newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK restaurant receipts seen growing stably - report.
newsitem.headline: HK restaurant receipts seen growing stably - report.

text.p: Hong Kong restaurant receipts are expected to show stable growth in the future, the Bank of East Asia Ltd said on Tuesday in a research report.

The short-term outlook of the industry is likely to be boosted by strong growth of private consumption and an influx of tourists around Hong Kong's reversion to China, which is expected to bring about HK$1.8 billion of receipts for the industry, it said.
Britain returns the colony to China at midnight of June 30.

"However, as the competition in the industry remains keen, restauranteurs' flexibiltity to increase prices will still be limited. Thus the overall growth of restaurant receipts is expected to be stable," it said.
The trend of a rising preference for eating out will also support the stable grwoth of restaurant receipts in the long term, the report said.
Total restaurant receipts in Hong Kong were provisionally HK$55.3 billion in 1996, a five percent rise over 1995, according to government data.
